title: VideoICEdit: Extending In-Context Instructional Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Diffusion Transformers
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains significantly harder than image editing due to the additional requirement of temporal consistency across frames. Existing video editing methods either require extensive fine-tuning on large video datasets or produce flickering artifacts when applied frame-by-frame. The in-context generation paradigm from ICEdit has not been explored for video, where temporal coherence constraints fundamentally change the editing dynamics.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video Diffusion Transformers (e.g., CogVideoX, Wan) by treating the original video and edited video as a paired in-context sequence along the temporal dimension. Specifically, we concatenate source and target video tokens spatiotemporally within the DiT's attention mechanism, enabling the model to leverage cross-frame and cross-video attention simultaneously. We introduce Temporal Consistency LoRA (TC-LoRA), a lightweight adapter trained on ~5K video-instruction pairs that jointly minimizes per-frame editing quality and inter-frame optical-flow consistency losses. Additionally, we propose a Temporal Early Filter that uses a VLM to score short candidate clips before full denoising, reducing inference cost.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly collected VideoEdit-100 benchmark measuring edit accuracy, temporal consistency (warping error), and identity preservation. We compare against Prompt2Prompt, TokenFlow, and InstructVideo baselines, demonstrating competitive performance with <0.5% trainable parameters and 1% of typical training data.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Consistent Instruction-Based Video Editing via Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging because existing methods struggle to maintain temporal consistency while applying semantically complex edits across frames, often requiring massive training datasets or suffering from flickering artifacts and identity drift between frames.

Proposed Method: We extend the ICEdit in-context generation paradigm to video diffusion transformers (e.g., CogVideoX or HunyuanVideo) by treating the editing problem as a multi-frame in-context generation task. Specifically, we concatenate a reference frame pair (original + edited anchor frame) with subsequent unedited frames in the spatiotemporal attention space, allowing the model to propagate edits consistently via its inherent in-context understanding. We introduce a Temporal Consistency LoRA (TC-LoRA) trained on a small curated video editing dataset (~5K clips) that encourages smooth edit propagation across time while preserving motion dynamics. Additionally, we propose Temporal Filter Inference-Time Scaling, which uses a VLM-based scorer to evaluate edit consistency and semantic accuracy across sampled keyframes before full decoding.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly collected benchmark of 200 diverse video editing prompts. Metrics include CLIP directional similarity, temporal consistency (warping error), identity preservation (DINO similarity), and human preference studies. We compare against TokenFlow, GroundedVideoEdit, and InstructVideo baselines, demonstrating competitive or superior performance with 1% training data.

title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instruction Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Editing via Frame-Pair Conditioning
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging because existing image editing methods applied frame-by-frame produce temporal flickering, while video-specific fine-tuning requires massive datasets and fails to leverage the strong semantic understanding of large diffusion models. ICEdit's in-context paradigm—conditioning on an original-edited image pair—has not been explored for maintaining temporal coherence across video frames.

Proposed Method: We extend ICEdit's in-context editing paradigm to video diffusion transformers (e.g., CogVideoX or Open-Sora) by designing a dual-stream in-context conditioning scheme. For each denoising step, we construct context tokens from (1) the first-frame original-edited pair (anchor pair) generated via ICEdit on the keyframe, and (2) temporally adjacent clean frames as additional context. We introduce lightweight temporal attention adapters (<1% parameters) that attend jointly to the in-context edit pair and neighboring frames, enforcing consistency without architectural overhaul. We further propose Temporal Filter Inference-Time Scaling, extending ICEdit's Early Filter mechanism to evaluate candidate noise samples using a VLM scoring both edit fidelity and optical-flow-based temporal smoothness.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly curated instruction-video benchmark across 5 editing categories (style, object, background, color, motion). Metrics include CLIP-based edit accuracy, temporal consistency (warping error), and FVD, comparing against Pix2Video, TokenFlow, and ground-truth fine-tuned baselines.

title: VideoICEdit: Temporal-Consistent Instructional Video Editing via In-Context Diffusion Transformers with Frame Coherence Scaling
description: Problem: Extending instruction-based editing from images to videos introduces a critical new challenge—temporal consistency across frames—while maintaining the precision-efficiency tradeoff addressed by ICEdit. Existing video editing methods either require massive video datasets or produce flickering artifacts when applied frame-by-frame. Proposed Method: We adapt ICEdit's in-context generation paradigm to video by constructing multi-frame in-context sequences where keyframes serve as anchors. Specifically, (1) we design a Temporal In-Context Window that concatenates the original video segment and partially-edited keyframes as context tokens within a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan), guiding coherent editing across all frames without architectural changes; (2) we introduce a lightweight Temporal LoRA (0.5% parameters) trained on <5K edited video clips that enforces motion-consistent edits; (3) we extend Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling with a Temporal Coherence Score using optical flow consistency as an additional VLM-agnostic quality signal to select temporally stable noise samples. Experiments: We evaluate on DAVIS-Edit and a new benchmark of 200 instruction-video pairs across color changes, object replacement, and style transfer. Metrics include CLIP-T, temporal warp error, and human preference studies, comparing against TokenFlow, Ground-A-Video, and frame-wise ICEdit baselines.

title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instruction Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Diffusion Transformers
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains vastly more challenging than image editing due to temporal consistency requirements. Existing video editing methods either require large-scale fine-tuning or produce flickering artifacts when applied frame-by-frame. The in-context paradigm from ICEdit has not been explored for video, where maintaining coherent edits across frames is critical.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video DiTs (e.g., CogVideoX, Wan) by treating the original video and edited video as paired temporal sequences within a single in-context generation pass. Specifically, we concatenate original and target video latents along the spatial (or batch) dimension, enabling the model's existing temporal attention to propagate edits consistently across frames. We introduce a Temporal Consistency LoRA (TC-LoRA) that fine-tunes only temporal attention layers (~0.5% parameters) to enforce coherent edits. Additionally, we propose Frame-Anchored Inference-Time Scaling, where a VLM scores candidate edits on keyframes before full generation, reducing wasted compute.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and a new benchmark of 500 instruction-edit video pairs across 10 edit categories. Metrics include CLIP-T (instruction alignment), warping error (temporal consistency), and FVD. We compare against Prompt2Prompt-Video, TokenFlow, and MotionDirector, demonstrating competitive quality with 100x less training data.

title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Editing via Temporal Attention Binding
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates impressive single-image editing with minimal training data, extending instruction-based editing to video remains challenging due to temporal consistency requirements—edits must propagate coherently across frames without flickering or semantic drift. Existing video editing methods require either massive video datasets or sacrifice temporal consistency for per-frame quality.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating a sequence of frames as a spatially-tiled in-context generation problem within a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan). We introduce Temporal Attention Binding (TAB), which anchors cross-frame attention to the edited reference frame generated at the first step, ensuring downstream frames inherit consistent structural and stylistic edits. We augment this with a lightweight temporal LoRA (0.5% trainable parameters) trained on synthetic video edit pairs created by applying ICEdit frame-by-frame and using optical flow to enforce temporal smoothness as supervision signal. Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling is adapted to select temporally stable noise trajectories using a VLM that scores edit consistency across sampled frame pairs.

Experiments: (1) TGVE and DAVIS benchmarks for temporal consistency metrics (warping error, CLIP consistency); (2) Instruction fidelity vs. frame count scaling; (3) Ablation of TAB vs. naive frame-independent editing; (4) Comparison against Tune-A-Video, TokenFlow, and ground-truth video editing baselines using only 500 video training examples.

title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instruction Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Editing via Frame-Pair Conditioning
description: Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging because existing methods either require expensive per-video fine-tuning or struggle to maintain temporal consistency across frames when applying semantic edits (e.g., 'make the car red', 'add snow to the scene'). Image editing paradigms like ICEdit cannot directly handle the temporal dimension. Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating video editing as a sequence of temporally-conditioned in-context generation tasks. Specifically, given an instruction and source video, we construct an in-context prompt where the first frame pair (source→edited) serves as a visual editing exemplar, generated via ICEdit. Subsequent frames are edited autoregressively, conditioning on both the in-context exemplar and the previously edited frame to enforce temporal coherence. We introduce a lightweight Temporal Attention Adapter (TAA) — a small set of cross-frame attention layers added to the frozen DiT backbone — trained on a small video editing dataset (~50K clips) to propagate edits consistently. Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling is adapted to select temporally coherent noise samples via a VLM scoring temporal consistency metrics. Experiments: We evaluate on DAVIS-Edit and a new benchmark (InstructVideo-100) measuring edit accuracy (CLIP-score), temporal consistency (warping error), and identity preservation (DINO similarity), comparing against Tokenflow, ControlVideo, and InstructPix2Pix-Video baselines.

title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instruction Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Diffusion Transformers
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging due to the need for temporal consistency across frames while responding accurately to natural language modifications. Existing video editing methods either require large-scale fine-tuning or produce flickering artifacts and poor instruction adherence. The in-context generation paradigm pioneered by ICEdit has not been explored for video, where temporal coherence introduces fundamentally new challenges.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video Diffusion Transformers (e.g., CogVideoX, Wan) by concatenating the original video latent sequence with a to-be-edited video latent along the spatial token dimension within the 3D attention mechanism, preserving the model's native temporal attention structure without architectural modifications. We introduce Temporal-Aware LoRA (TA-LoRA), which applies parameter-efficient fine-tuning selectively to temporal attention layers to enforce cross-frame consistency. Additionally, we propose a Temporal Coherence Filter for inference-time scaling, using a VLM to score candidate generations on both edit quality and inter-frame consistency.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC video editing benchmarks, measuring temporal consistency (CLIP-T score across frames), edit accuracy (instruction-following rate), and perceptual quality (FVD). Ablations compare TA-LoRA vs. full fine-tuning, with and without the temporal coherence filter, using <50K training video clips.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Consistent Instruction-Based Video Editing via Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging due to temporal consistency requirements—existing methods either fine-tune heavily on large video datasets or apply frame-by-frame image editing that produces flickering artifacts and semantic drift across frames. Extending ICEdit's efficient in-context paradigm to video editing could enable temporally coherent modifications with minimal training data.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video DiTs (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan) by reformulating temporal video editing as a multi-frame in-context generation problem. Specifically, we construct an in-context sequence where keyframes from the original video and a text instruction jointly condition generation of the edited video. We introduce Temporal Attention Anchoring (TAA), which selectively freezes temporal attention layers while fine-tuning only spatial cross-attention parameters (~0.5% of weights), preserving motion consistency while adapting appearance. We further propose Temporal Early Filter Scaling, using a VLM to score candidate edited sequences for both instruction adherence and inter-frame consistency before selecting final outputs.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks measuring (1) instruction following accuracy, (2) temporal consistency (CLIP frame similarity, warping error), and (3) training efficiency (dataset size, compute). Ablations isolate TAA contributions versus naive frame-independent ICEdit application, demonstrating that our approach achieves state-of-the-art video editing with <1K training video clips.

title: ConsistentICEdit: Maintaining Identity and Style Coherence Across Multi-Step Instructional Editing Sequences
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates impressive single-step instruction-based editing, real-world workflows often require sequential, multi-step edits (e.g., 'change hair color' → 'add glasses' → 'change background'). Existing methods, including ICEdit, suffer from accumulated drift—each editing step degrades attributes from prior steps, causing identity inconsistency and stylistic incoherence across editing chains. Proposed Method: We introduce ConsistentICEdit, which extends the in-context generation paradigm to multi-step editing sequences by maintaining a 'context memory buffer'—a compact latent representation storing the cumulative editing history. At each step, the diffusion transformer receives both the current image and a compressed context embedding of all prior edits via cross-attention, preventing catastrophic forgetting of preserved attributes. We further propose a Consistency Regularization Loss that penalizes deviation in identity-critical regions (detected via face/object segmentation) across editing steps. The approach remains parameter-efficient by fine-tuning only lightweight adapter layers on sequential editing trajectories synthesized from existing datasets. Experiments: We construct a new benchmark, MultiEditBench, with 500 images requiring 3-7 sequential edits with ground-truth references. We evaluate identity preservation (FaceNet similarity), instruction fidelity (CLIP score), and accumulated drift (per-step SSIM on preserved regions) against ICEdit, InstructPix2Pix, and Emu-Edit baselines.

title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instruction Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Modification via Sparse Keyframe Conditioning
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging because existing image editing methods applied frame-by-frame produce temporal flickering and inconsistency, while dedicated video editing models require enormous training data and compute. The success of ICEdit's in-context paradigm for images suggests a natural extension to video, but naive application ignores temporal dependencies.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating a sparse set of keyframes as in-context exemplars within a video Diffusion Transformer (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan). Specifically, we construct a keyframe-conditioned in-context sequence where the source keyframe and its edited counterpart (produced by ICEdit) serve as a visual instruction pair, and intermediate frames are generated conditioned on both this pair and neighboring frames. We introduce Temporal Attention Anchoring (TAA), a lightweight LoRA adaptation (~1% parameters) that injects temporal consistency by attending edited keyframes as anchors during non-keyframe denoising. Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling is extended to select temporally coherent noise initializations via a VLM scoring both edit fidelity and optical-flow consistency.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly collected instruction video editing benchmark across 5 edit categories (color, texture, style, object replacement, background). Metrics include frame-wise CLIP similarity, temporal consistency (warping error), and user studies comparing against Prompt2Prompt, TokenFlow, and InstructVideo, targeting SOTA with <1% trainable parameters.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Editing to Consistent Video Sequences via Diffusion Transformer Propagation
description: Problem: Instruction-based editing of videos remains challenging because maintaining temporal consistency across frames while applying semantic edits (e.g., 'make the sky stormy' or 'change the car color to red') requires both strong language comprehension and coherent propagation across time. Existing video editing methods either fine-tune heavily or apply per-frame image editing with flickering artifacts. Method: We extend the ICEdit in-context paradigm to video by treating temporal sequences as extended in-context windows within video-capable Diffusion Transformers (e.g., CogVideoX or Open-Sora). Specifically, we propose (1) a keyframe anchor strategy where edited keyframes serve as in-context exemplars for propagating edits to intermediate frames; (2) a lightweight temporal attention adapter (< 2% trainable parameters) that enforces cross-frame feature consistency without full fine-tuning; and (3) an inference-time scaling mechanism that samples multiple edit candidates per keyframe and selects the most temporally coherent sequence using a VLM-based consistency scorer. Experiments: We benchmark on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly curated instructional video editing dataset. Metrics include temporal consistency (CLIP cosine similarity across frames), instruction adherence (GPT-4V scoring), and FVD. We compare against TokenFlow, CoDeF, and Pix2Video baselines, demonstrating competitive quality with 10x less training data.

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Instruction Following
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation within Diffusion Transformers enables efficient image editing, extending instruction-based editing to video remains challenging due to temporal consistency requirements — edits must remain coherent across frames without flickering or semantic drift. Existing video editing methods require even larger datasets and compute than their image counterparts, making the efficiency gains of ICEdit especially valuable in this domain. Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating the original video and edited output as temporally-paired in-context sequences within a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or Open-Sora). We introduce a Temporal Attention Anchoring mechanism that ties in-context attention tokens across frames, enforcing edit consistency without architectural overhaul. We apply LoRA fine-tuning on only temporal attention layers (<0.5% parameters) using a small paired video-instruction dataset (~5K clip pairs) constructed via automated pipeline from existing image editing datasets through frame interpolation. Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling is adapted to score temporal coherence via a VLM that evaluates cross-frame semantic stability. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks measuring edit accuracy (CLIP similarity), temporal consistency (warping error), and background preservation (PSNR), comparing against Tune-A-Video, TokenFlow, and ground-truth image editing baselines applied frame-wise.

title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instructional Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Editing via Sparse Frame Conditioning
description: Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging due to the need for temporal consistency across frames while maintaining precise semantic edits. Existing video editing methods require either massive training data or sacrifice temporal coherence when adapting image editing approaches frame-by-frame. Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm from ICEdit to video diffusion transformers (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan) by introducing a sparse keyframe in-context conditioning scheme. Specifically, we treat (original_keyframe, edited_keyframe) pairs as in-context examples within the video DiT's joint attention space, allowing non-keyframes to attend to these edited references and propagate edits temporally without architectural modifications. We additionally introduce a Temporal Consistency LoRA (TC-LoRA) trained on only ~5K edited video clips, penalizing optical-flow-weighted feature discrepancies between adjacent frames. At inference time, we apply VLM-guided filtering analogous to ICEdit's Early Filter scaling, but operating on sampled keyframe edits before full video generation. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly curated benchmark of 500 instruction-video pairs across object replacement, style transfer, and attribute editing. Metrics include CLIP-Text alignment, temporal consistency (warping error), and human preference studies, comparing against Pix2Video, TokenFlow, and MotionDirector baselines.

title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instruction Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Editing via Sparse Frame Anchoring
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging because existing methods either require massive training datasets or fail to maintain temporal consistency across frames. While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation within DiTs enables efficient image editing, extending this paradigm to video introduces the critical challenge of ensuring coherent edits across hundreds of frames without per-frame drift.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video DiTs (e.g., CogVideoX, Wan) by introducing Sparse Frame Anchoring (SFA). Rather than editing all frames independently, we select K keyframes and apply ICEdit-style in-context generation, treating the original-keyframe pairs as context tokens. Intermediate frames are then edited using cross-frame attention injection from neighboring keyframe edit pairs, propagating structural and semantic edits temporally. We apply LoRA fine-tuning (~1% parameters) on a small paired video-instruction dataset (~5K clips) to improve temporal coherence. Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling is adapted to score candidate edits based on both per-frame quality and optical-flow consistency.

Experiments: (1) TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks for temporal consistency and editing accuracy; (2) Ablation on number of keyframes K; (3) Comparison against Pix2Video, TokenFlow, and InstructVideo; (4) User study on coherence vs. edit fidelity tradeoff. We target state-of-the-art performance with <1K training videos.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Consistent Instruction-Based Video Editing via Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates remarkable efficiency for single-image instruction-based editing using in-context generation in DiTs, extending this paradigm to video editing remains unsolved. Video editing demands temporal consistency across frames — a challenge that naive per-frame application of ICEdit fails to address, producing flickering artifacts and inconsistent edits.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating spatiotemporal attention in video DiTs (e.g., CogVideoX, Wan) as the backbone. Specifically, (1) we design a keyframe-anchored in-context layout, placing edited keyframes alongside unedited intermediate frames within the video DiT's joint attention window; (2) we introduce lightweight temporal LoRA adapters (<<1% parameters) trained on a small paired video editing dataset (~5K clips) to preserve temporal coherence; (3) we apply VLM-based Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling across multiple candidate noise trajectories to select temporally consistent edits.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, FreSCo-Vid, and a new benchmark of 500 instruction-annotated video clips. Metrics include CLIP-Text alignment, temporal consistency (CLIP frame similarity), and FVD. Ablations analyze keyframe density, LoRA rank, and scaling budget.

title: ChainEdit: Multi-Step Instructional Image Editing via Sequential In-Context Chaining in Diffusion Transformers
description: Problem: Current instruction-based editing methods, including ICEdit, excel at single-step edits but struggle with complex multi-step editing sequences (e.g., 'remove the hat, change shirt color to red, add sunglasses, place in a snowy background'). Naively chaining single-step edits accumulates artifacts and semantic drift across iterations, degrading image quality progressively. Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to multi-step sequential editing by introducing a context-aware chaining mechanism within DiTs. Each editing step conditions on a growing in-context window containing the original image and all intermediate edited states, allowing the model to maintain global semantic consistency. We propose a 'consistency anchor loss' during parameter-efficient fine-tuning that penalizes deviation from unedited regions across the chain. Additionally, we introduce a step-aware Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling that uses VLMs to evaluate not just individual step quality but cumulative coherence across the editing chain. Experiments: We construct a multi-step editing benchmark (MultiEditBench) with 500 sequences of 3-6 chained instructions across diverse domains. We evaluate against baselines (sequential InstructPix2Pix, sequential ICEdit, Prompt2Prompt chaining) using CLIP consistency, human preference scores, and a novel Cumulative Drift Metric measuring semantic fidelity to the original subject across steps.

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequence Modification
description:
Problem: Instruction-based editing of video sequences remains challenging because existing image editing methods (including ICEdit) treat frames independently, causing temporal flickering and inconsistent edits across frames. Fine-tuning video diffusion models requires enormous datasets, while training-free approaches lack instruction comprehension.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by formulating temporal consistency as an additional in-context constraint. Specifically, we arrange keyframes alongside a reference edited frame (generated by ICEdit on the first frame) in a spatiotemporal context window fed into a video DiT. A lightweight temporal attention adapter (< 2% trainable parameters) learns to propagate edit coherence across frames using only a small dataset of ~50K short video clips with paired edit instructions. We introduce Temporal Edit Consistency Score (TECS), combining per-frame edit fidelity with optical-flow-based warp consistency between consecutive edited frames.

Experiments: (1) Quantitative comparison against vid2vid-zero, TokenFlow, and Ground-A-Video on DAVIS and a newly curated VideoEdit-100 benchmark using TECS, CLIP-Score, and temporal warp error; (2) Ablation of context window size and adapter rank; (3) User study on naturalness and instruction fidelity; (4) Scaling analysis showing edit quality vs. number of keyframes in context. We expect state-of-the-art temporal consistency with <5K training videos.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Diffusion Transformers to Consistent Video Editing
description:

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Editing to Consistent Video Sequences via Diffusion Transformer Memory
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that large-scale Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) can perform instruction-based image editing with minimal training data and parameters, extending this paradigm to video editing remains challenging due to temporal consistency requirements — edits must propagate coherently across frames without flickering or content drift. Existing video editing methods either require extensive fine-tuning or struggle to maintain edit consistency over time.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating temporal frames as an extended in-context sequence within the DiT architecture. Specifically, we concatenate a reference frame (original) with its edited counterpart as in-context anchors, then process subsequent frames conditioned on this anchor pair. We introduce a Temporal Attention Binding module — a lightweight LoRA adaptation (~0.5% parameters) — that propagates edit signals across frames while preserving motion dynamics. An Optical Flow Consistency loss during fine-tuning enforces temporal smoothness. A VLM-guided keyframe selection strategy extends ICEdit's Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling to identify frames requiring stronger edit guidance.

Experiments: We evaluate on DAVIS, BalanceCC, and a newly collected instructional video editing benchmark (100 videos, 15 edit categories). Metrics include CLIP-consistency across frames, edit fidelity (CLIPScore), temporal warp error, and user studies comparing against TokenFlow, Pix2Video, and Ground-A-Video, using only 5K training video clips.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Consistent Instruction-Based Video Editing via Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation in Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) enables efficient image editing, extending this paradigm to video remains unsolved. Video editing requires temporal consistency across frames alongside precise instruction following — existing video editing methods either require extensive fine-tuning on large video datasets or produce flickering artifacts from frame-independent editing.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating a sequence of (original frame, edited frame) pairs as an in-context sequence within a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or Open-Sora). Specifically: (1) We construct a 'temporal in-context token layout' where alternating original and edited frames are concatenated along the sequence dimension, allowing the model to infer temporal-consistent edits from the instruction; (2) We introduce a lightweight temporal consistency adapter (LoRA-based, <2% parameters) trained on a small set of paired video clips (~5K videos) to enforce cross-frame coherence; (3) We propose Temporal Early Filter Scaling — using a VLM to score candidate edits for both edit quality AND inter-frame consistency before selection.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks measuring edit accuracy, temporal consistency (warping error), and frame quality (CLIP score). Ablations compare with per-frame ICEdit application, TokenFlow, and ground-truth supervised baselines.

title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instruction Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Sequences via Frame-Pair Conditioning
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains computationally prohibitive and temporally inconsistent. Existing methods either fine-tune massive video diffusion models or apply image editing frame-by-frame without enforcing temporal coherence. ICEdit's in-context paradigm—placing source and target images side-by-side as context—offers a lightweight blueprint, but naive extension to video ignores inter-frame dependencies.

Proposed Method: We extend ICEdit's in-context paradigm to video Diffusion Transformers (e.g., CogVideoX or Open-Sora) by treating consecutive frame pairs as spatiotemporal context tokens. Specifically, we concatenate (source_frame_t, source_frame_{t+1}, target_frame_t) as conditioning context, and predict target_frame_{t+1} autoregressively. A lightweight temporal attention adapter (~1% parameters) is fine-tuned on a small paired video-edit dataset (~50K clips generated via ICEdit on video frames). We introduce Temporal Filter Inference-Time Scaling, extending ICEdit's Early Filter mechanism with a VLM scoring both visual quality and optical-flow consistency between predicted consecutive edited frames.

Experiments: (1) Quantitative comparison on TGVE and DAVIS benchmarks using temporal consistency (warping error), editing fidelity (CLIP-T), and efficiency metrics; (2) Ablation on temporal adapter design and context window size; (3) User study on coherence vs. per-frame ICEdit baselines; (4) Analysis of scaling inference-time compute via temporal filtering on editing quality.

title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Temporal Editing to Video Diffusion Transformers via Sparse Keyframe Conditioning
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains severely underexplored compared to image editing. Existing video editing methods either require extensive fine-tuning on large video datasets or fail to maintain temporal consistency across frames when applying localized edits. The core challenge is propagating precise, instruction-guided edits coherently through time without per-video optimization.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context generation paradigm from ICEdit to video diffusion transformers (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan). Our approach, ICVideoEdit, treats video editing as a sparse keyframe in-context problem: (1) we select K keyframes and concatenate each with a blank target slot in the spatial token sequence, forming an in-context editing sequence; (2) a lightweight LoRA adapter trained on ~50K video-instruction pairs enforces temporal attention consistency between edited keyframes; (3) an optical-flow-guided interpolation module propagates keyframe edits to intermediate frames while respecting motion boundaries; (4) an Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling mechanism uses a video-language model to score temporal coherence of candidate denoised samples.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly curated VideoEdit-50K benchmark measuring edit accuracy (CLIP-score), temporal consistency (frame-to-frame SSIM), and identity preservation (DINO similarity), comparing against Tune-A-Video, TokenFlow, and ground-truth supervised baselines.

title: Temporal ICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Instruction Following
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation within Diffusion Transformers enables efficient image editing, extending this paradigm to video remains unsolved. Video editing requires temporal consistency across frames—a property that naive per-frame application of ICEdit violates, producing flickering artifacts and inconsistent edits. Proposed Method: We propose Temporal ICEdit, which adapts the in-context editing paradigm to video DiTs (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan) by concatenating a reference edited frame alongside the source video frames in the temporal attention context. Specifically, we: (1) apply ICEdit to generate a single high-quality anchor frame edit, (2) propagate this edit across all frames by conditioning the video DiT's temporal attention on the anchor (source, edited) pair as in-context tokens, and (3) introduce a lightweight temporal consistency LoRA trained on <50K video clips that learns to respect the in-context temporal signal without architectural changes. Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling is extended to select temporally coherent noise trajectories via a video-aware VLM scorer. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly curated benchmark of 500 instruction-edit video pairs, measuring CLIP-T, temporal consistency (Warp Error), and human preference. Baselines include TokenFlow, FLATTEN, and ground-truth supervised methods.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequences
description:

Existing video editing methods either require per-video fine-tuning or struggle to maintain instruction fidelity over time.

We further extend Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling to select temporally coherent noise trajectories via a VLM-based consistency scorer.

Comparisons against Tune-A-Video, TokenFlow, and ground-truth fine-tuned baselines validate efficiency-quality tradeoffs.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Consistent Instruction-Guided Video Editing via Diffusion Transformers
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation within DiTs enables efficient image editing, extending this paradigm to video remains unsolved. Video editing requires not only accurate per-frame instruction following but also temporal consistency across frames — a challenge that existing methods address poorly without massive video-text paired datasets.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating a video clip as a sequence of frame pairs (original frame, edited frame) arranged in a spatiotemporal context window within a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or Open-Sora). We propose Temporal In-Context Editing (TICEdit), which: (1) arranges sparse keyframe pairs as in-context exemplars within the video DiT's 3D attention, allowing the model to propagate edits coherently to intermediate frames; (2) introduces a lightweight temporal attention adapter (LoRA on temporal attention layers only, ~0.5% parameters) fine-tuned on fewer than 5K video-instruction pairs; (3) applies a temporally-aware inference-time scaling strategy that filters candidate edits based on optical-flow consistency scores using a lightweight VLM judge.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly curated video editing benchmark. Metrics include CLIP-Text alignment, temporal consistency (CLIP cosine similarity across frames), warping error, and LPIPS against ground-truth edits. Baselines include TokenFlow, Pix2Video, and InstructVideo.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Diffusion Transformers to Consistent Video Editing with Minimal Fine-Tuning
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation within large-scale DiTs enables efficient image editing with minimal data and parameters, extending this paradigm to video editing remains unsolved. Video editing requires temporal consistency across frames, but naive per-frame application of image editing methods produces flickering artifacts and semantic drift. Existing video editing approaches require even larger datasets and compute than their image counterparts. Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by introducing Temporal In-Context Editing (TICEdit). We treat a video as a sequence of frame tokens within a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or HunyuanVideo), constructing an in-context prompt by concatenating a reference frame pair (original + edited keyframe produced by ICEdit) alongside the full original video sequence. Temporal self-attention naturally propagates the edit instruction across frames. We apply LoRA fine-tuning (~1% parameters) on a small dataset of ~5K edited video clips and introduce Temporal Early Filter Scaling, using a VLM to score temporal consistency and edit fidelity across candidate generations. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks measuring temporal consistency (CLIP-T), edit accuracy, and frame quality (PSNR/SSIM), comparing against Tune-A-Video, TokenFlow, and ground-truth upper bounds, demonstrating competitive performance with <1% of typical training data.

title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation to Temporal Instruction-Based Video Editing
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains costly and imprecise—existing methods require either massive video datasets for fine-tuning or struggle to maintain temporal consistency across frames while following complex natural language edits. ICEdit's success in image editing via in-context generation suggests an unexplored opportunity to extend this paradigm to the video domain.

Proposed Method: We propose ICVideoEdit, which reformulates instruction-based video editing as a spatio-temporal in-context generation task within large-scale video Diffusion Transformers (e.g., CogVideoX, HunyuanVideo). The approach concatenates a reference frame pair (original + edited exemplar, generated via ICEdit) alongside the target video frames within the transformer's context window, enabling the model to infer consistent temporal edits without architectural changes. We introduce a Temporal Attention Anchor mechanism that propagates editing signals across frames via cross-frame attention reweighting. Parameter-efficient LoRA fine-tuning (~1% parameters) on a small curated dataset (~50K clips) stabilizes temporal coherence. An Inference-Time Temporal Filter uses a VLM to score frame-level edit quality and consistency, selecting optimal noise trajectories.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and a new benchmark (TemporalEditBench) measuring edit accuracy, temporal consistency (CLIP-T), and flicker metrics. Baselines include InstructVideo, TokenFlow, and Ground-A-Video. Ablations study context window size, exemplar quality, and LoRA rank effects on temporal coherence.

title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instructional Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Diffusion Transformers
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains far more challenging than image editing due to the need for temporal consistency across frames, yet existing video editing methods either require massive training datasets or produce flickering artifacts when applied frame-by-frame. Current in-context generation paradigms like ICEdit operate only on static images and lack mechanisms to enforce cross-frame coherence.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video DiTs (e.g., CogVideoX, HunyuanVideo) by treating the original video and edited video as paired temporal contexts within a single forward pass. Specifically, we concatenate source and target video tokens along the spatial dimension at each timestep, enabling the model to attend jointly to all frames of both videos simultaneously. We introduce Temporal Consistency LoRA (TC-LoRA), a lightweight adapter (~1% parameters) trained on a small curated dataset (~50K video-instruction pairs) that learns to enforce cross-frame attention alignment. Additionally, we propose Temporal Early Filter Scaling, using a video-language model to score temporal coherence of candidate denoised trajectories during inference.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE, BalanceCC, and a newly constructed VideoEditBench covering 200 diverse edit types. Metrics include CLIP-Text alignment, temporal consistency (CLIP-T), identity preservation (DINO), and human preference studies. Ablations isolate TC-LoRA vs. vanilla LoRA and temporal filtering contributions.

title: Temporal ICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Instruction Following
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates remarkable efficiency for single-image editing, extending instruction-based editing to video remains challenging due to temporal consistency requirements — edits must propagate coherently across frames without flickering or semantic drift. title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Temporal Editing to Diffusion Transformer Video Models
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation enables efficient image editing in DiTs, extending this paradigm to video editing remains unexplored. Video editing introduces temporal consistency challenges — edits must propagate coherently across frames without flickering or semantic drift — that static image methods cannot address. Existing video editing methods similarly suffer from the precision-efficiency tradeoff, requiring large datasets or sacrificing instruction fidelity.

Proposed Method: We propose IC-VideoEdit, which adapts the in-context editing paradigm to video DiTs (e.g., CogVideoX or Open-Sora). The method concatenates the source video and a partially-noised target video along the sequence dimension within the existing attention mechanism, exploiting the video DiT's native temporal attention to propagate edits consistently across frames. We introduce Temporal Anchor Tokens — a small set of learnable tokens (0.5% of parameters) that explicitly enforce cross-frame edit coherence during fine-tuning on a minimal dataset (~5K edited video pairs). We further extend Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling by using a VLM to score temporal consistency alongside edit accuracy across sampled denoising trajectories.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks measuring frame consistency (CLIP cosine similarity), edit accuracy, and temporal warping error. Ablations isolate contributions of temporal anchor tokens, in-context concatenation axis choices, and inference-time scaling on video quality versus compute tradeoffs.

title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Transformer Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Sequences
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation within DiTs enables efficient single-image editing with minimal training data, extending this paradigm to video editing remains unsolved. Video editing requires temporal consistency across frames—naive per-frame application of in-context editing produces flickering artifacts and inconsistent modifications. Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating a temporal window of frames as a structured in-context sequence within the DiT. Specifically, we arrange triplets of (reference frame, instruction embedding, target frame) across multiple timesteps as a spatiotemporal in-context grid, enabling the attention mechanism to naturally propagate edits while maintaining cross-frame coherence. We introduce Temporal Attention Anchoring (TAA), a lightweight LoRA adaptation (~1% parameters) trained on a small video-instruction dataset (~50K clips) that encourages consistent token activations across the temporal dimension. Additionally, we propose a temporal variant of Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling where a video-language model scores candidate noise trajectories for both edit quality and inter-frame consistency. Ablations compare per-frame ICEdit baselines, optical-flow warping alternatives, and full-video fine-tuning approaches, demonstrating competitive temporal coherence with 0.5% of typical video editing training data.

title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Temporal Editing via Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation
description: Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains underexplored compared to image editing, with existing methods requiring massive video datasets and struggling to maintain temporal consistency while accurately following natural language edits. The ICEdit paradigm demonstrated that in-context generation in Diffusion Transformers enables efficient image editing, but extending this to video introduces new challenges: temporal coherence across frames and the combinatorial explosion of noise sampling for sequences. Proposed Method: We propose IC-VideoEdit, which extends the in-context editing paradigm to video by concatenating a source video clip with a partially denoised target sequence in the spatial-temporal attention of a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan). We introduce Temporal In-Context Tokens that represent the source video as a compressed set of conditioning frames alongside the edit instruction, enabling parameter-efficient LoRA fine-tuning on only ~1K video edit pairs. We further propose Temporal Early Filter Scaling, where a VLM evaluates intermediate denoised frames to prune low-fidelity generation trajectories early, improving efficiency. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and a newly curated VideoEditBench across metrics including temporal consistency (CLIP-T), edit fidelity (CLIPScore), and video quality (FVD), comparing against InstructVideo, TokenFlow, and ground-truth supervised baselines, targeting competitive performance with <0.5% trainable parameters.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Editing to Consistent Video Sequences via Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation in Diffusion Transformers enables efficient image editing, extending this paradigm to video remains unsolved. Video editing requires temporal consistency across frames—a challenge where existing methods either process frames independently (causing flickering) or require massive video-specific training datasets. Proposed Method: We propose TemporalICEdit, which extends the in-context editing paradigm to video by concatenating a source-frame/edited-frame pair (the 'editing context') alongside multiple target video frames within a single DiT forward pass. Specifically, we arrange tokens as [source_frame | edited_reference | target_frame_t | target_frame_t+1 | ...] leveraging the DiT's attention mechanism to naturally propagate editing instructions across frames. We introduce a lightweight temporal attention adapter (< 2% trainable parameters) fine-tuned on a small synthetic video editing dataset (~50K clips) to enforce cross-frame consistency without disrupting the pretrained in-context editing capability. An optical-flow-guided attention mask prevents temporal bleeding between non-adjacent frames. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and CelebV-Text benchmarks measuring frame consistency (CLIP cosine similarity between frames), edit fidelity (CLIP-I score), and temporal flickering (warping error). Ablations examine context window size, adapter placement, and attention masking strategies. Baselines include Tokenflow, FLATTEN, and per-frame ICEdit.

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Transformers for Consistent Multi-Frame Video Editing via Instruction Prompts
description: Problem: Instruction-based editing of video content requires maintaining temporal consistency across frames while applying semantically meaningful edits — a challenge existing image-focused methods like ICEdit cannot address, and video-specific approaches require prohibitively large training datasets. title: ICEdit-Video: Extending In-Context Instruction Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Editing via Frame-Pair Conditioning
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging because existing methods either require expensive per-video fine-tuning or produce temporally inconsistent edits across frames. While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation in Diffusion Transformers enables efficient image editing, extending this to video introduces the additional constraint of temporal coherence.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by constructing multi-frame in-context sequences where the input to the DiT interleaves (original frame, edited frame) pairs across time. Specifically, we leverage a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan) and construct context windows containing: (1) an anchor in-context pair (original→edited) generated via ICEdit for the first frame, and (2) subsequent original frames requiring editing, conditioning the model to propagate edits temporally. We introduce Temporal Attention Modulation (TAM), a lightweight LoRA adapter (~0.5% parameters) that reinforces cross-frame edit consistency without full fine-tuning. Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling is adapted to score full clip candidates using a video-language model.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks measuring edit fidelity (CLIP-T), temporal consistency (CLIP frame similarity), and background preservation (PSNR). We compare against Tokenflow, Ground-A-Video, and InstructVideo using only ~50K video clip pairs for training, targeting 10× data efficiency over baselines.

title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Transformer Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Sequences

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Instruction Following

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Editing to Consistent Video Sequence Modification via Diffusion Transformers
description:

title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending In-Context Generation Paradigms to Temporally Consistent Instructional Video Editing
description:

title: VideoICEdit: Extending In-Context Instructional Editing to Temporally Consistent Video Diffusion Transformers

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Editing to Video via Sparse Keyframe Conditioning in Diffusion Transformers
description:

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequences

title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Sequences

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequence Modification via Temporal Attention Anchoring

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Transformers for Consistent Multi-Frame Video Editing via Instruction Sequences

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks measuring edit fidelity (CLIP-based), temporal consistency (warping error), and background preservation. Ablations test keyframe density, adapter size, and scaling budget. title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Instructional Editing to Temporal Sequences via Sparse Keyframe In-Context Generation

title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Editing to Temporal Consistency via Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation
description: Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains challenging because methods must maintain temporal consistency across frames while precisely following natural language edits. Existing video editing approaches either require extensive fine-tuning on large video datasets or struggle with frame-to-frame coherence when adapted from image editing paradigms. title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Temporal Editing to Diffusion Video Transformers via In-Context Frame Generation
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates remarkable efficiency for image editing via in-context generation in DiTs, extending this paradigm to video editing remains unsolved. Video editing requires temporal consistency across frames, understanding of motion-related instructions (e.g., 'make the person walk faster', 'add rain to the scene'), and handling of long-range dependencies — challenges absent in single-image editing. Existing video editing methods either require extensive fine-tuning on large video datasets or suffer from temporal flickering and poor instruction comprehension. Proposed Method: We propose IC-VideoEdit, which adapts the in-context editing paradigm to video DiT architectures (e.g., CogVideoX, HunyuanVideo). Our approach concatenates a reference frame pair (original + edited frame, generated via ICEdit) alongside the target video sequence as temporal in-context conditioning. We introduce Temporal Attention Anchoring (TAA), a lightweight LoRA-based fine-tuning targeting only temporal attention layers (~0.5% parameters), to enforce cross-frame consistency. An early-exit temporal coherence filter using a VLM scores candidate noise trajectories for both edit quality and temporal smoothness. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC-Video benchmarks, measuring temporal consistency (warping error), edit accuracy (CLIP scores), and efficiency vs. TokenFlow, Ground-A-Video, and Video-P2P baselines, demonstrating competitive quality with <1% of their training data.

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Transformers for Consistent Multi-Frame Video Editing via Instruction-Guided Temporal Attention
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation within Diffusion Transformers enables efficient single-image editing, extending this paradigm to video remains unsolved. Video editing requires not only accurate instruction following per frame but also temporal consistency across frames — a challenge where existing methods either process frames independently (causing flickering) or require expensive video-specific training.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating a temporal window of frames as an extended in-context sequence within the DiT. Specifically, we concatenate source-frame pairs across T frames (e.g., T=8) along the sequence dimension, allowing the transformer's self-attention to simultaneously reason about instruction semantics and inter-frame consistency. We introduce lightweight Temporal LoRA adapters (expanding ICEdit's 1% parameter budget by ~0.5%) that modulate attention between corresponding frame positions, encouraging coherent edits. We further extend Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling to a temporal coherence score using optical flow consistency between VLM-selected candidates.

Experiments: (1) Evaluate on DAVIS-Edit and a new instruction-video editing benchmark we construct from TGVE; (2) Compare against TokenFlow, Prompt-to-Prompt video extensions, and ground-truth video editing baselines; (3) Ablate temporal window size, LoRA placement, and temporal coherence filtering; (4) Measure CLIP-Text alignment, warping error (temporal consistency), and human preference scores.

title: TemporalEdit: In-Context Video Editing via Sparse Frame Conditioning in Diffusion Transformers
description: Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains computationally prohibitive and temporally inconsistent. Existing methods either fine-tune on massive video datasets or apply per-frame image editing without enforcing temporal coherence. ICEdit's success in leveraging DiT in-context generation for images suggests a natural extension to video, but naively tiling frames in context windows ignores temporal structure and blows up attention complexity. Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by introducing sparse keyframe conditioning. Rather than including all frames in the context, we select K representative keyframes (via scene-change detection or uniform sampling) and construct an in-context sequence pairing each keyframe with its edited version. Remaining frames are generated conditioned on neighboring edited keyframes via temporal attention interpolation within the DiT backbone. We apply lightweight LoRA fine-tuning (~1% parameters) on a small video editing dataset (~50K clips) to teach temporal consistency. An Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling step uses a VLM to evaluate edit quality and motion smoothness across candidate outputs. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and EvalCrafter benchmarks measuring edit accuracy (CLIP similarity), temporal consistency (warping error), and efficiency (training data/FLOPs) against InstructVideo, TokenFlow, and ground-truth supervised methods. Ablations examine keyframe density and LoRA rank effects on coherence.

title: VideoICEdit: Extending In-Context Instructional Editing to Temporal Video Sequences via Frame-Coherent Diffusion Transformers
description: Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains far more challenging than image editing due to the need for temporal consistency across frames. Existing video editing methods either require expensive fine-tuning on large video datasets or suffer from flickering artifacts and semantic drift when applied frame-by-frame. Specifically, we propose a 'temporal in-context strip' that arranges keyframes alongside the original video frames within the model's native attention space, enabling cross-frame instruction comprehension without architectural changes. We introduce Temporal Attention Anchoring (TAA), a lightweight LoRA fine-tuning strategy (~1% parameters) that conditions inter-frame attention on instruction tokens to enforce temporal coherence. Additionally, we adapt Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling to video by scoring candidate noise trajectories using a VLM that evaluates both per-frame quality and inter-frame consistency. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalancedEdit-Video benchmarks measuring temporal consistency (CLIP-T cosine similarity across frames), editing fidelity (GPT-4V scoring), and computational cost versus baselines including TokenFlow, Ground-A-Video, and frame-wise ICEdit. Ablations isolate contributions of TAA and temporal scaling.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Diffusion Transformers to Consistent Video Editing with Minimal Fine-Tuning
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains significantly harder than image editing due to the need for temporal consistency across frames. Existing video editing methods either require extensive fine-tuning on large video datasets or produce flickering, inconsistent edits across frames. The input context consists of (original frame sequence, instruction token, blank target sequence), where the DiT attends across both spatial and temporal axes. We introduce Temporal Attention Anchoring (TAA), a lightweight LoRA adaptation (targeting <2% parameters) that enforces cross-frame consistency by tying attention patterns between adjacent frames during in-context generation. An inference-time scaling strategy selects temporally coherent noise initializations using a VLM scoring consistency across sampled candidates.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC video editing benchmarks measuring frame-level edit accuracy (CLIP-I, CLIP-T), temporal consistency (Warp Error, DINO cosine similarity across frames), and efficiency (training data/compute). title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Sequences
description:

Existing video editing methods either require expensive full fine-tuning or struggle to maintain coherent edits across temporally adjacent frames when applying instruction-based modifications.

Specifically, we concatenate a reference (original) frame alongside K temporally sampled video frames as a joint context window, allowing the model to attend across both the edit instruction context and temporal neighbors simultaneously. We introduce lightweight temporal attention adapters (LoRA-style, <2% parameters) trained on a small paired video-edit dataset (~50K clips) to encourage cross-frame consistency. We further adapt Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling by using a video-VLM to score temporal coherence alongside edit quality during noise sampling.

title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Clip Modification
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates remarkable efficiency for single-image instruction-based editing, extending instructional editing to video clips remains challenging due to temporal consistency requirements — naive per-frame editing produces flickering artifacts and breaks object/lighting coherence across frames. Existing video editing methods require even larger datasets and more computation than single-image counterparts.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to short video clips (4-16 frames) by constructing a temporal in-context window: instead of a single (source, target) image pair, the model conditions on a sequence of source frames concatenated with partially-completed target frames in a sliding attention window within a video DiT backbone (e.g., CogVideoX or Open-Sora). We introduce Temporal Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (T-PEFT), adding lightweight temporal attention adapters (~1% parameters) trained on a small paired video editing dataset (~50K clips) synthesized via ICEdit applied to existing video datasets. An Optical-Flow-Guided Consistency Loss penalizes inter-frame feature drift during fine-tuning.

Experiments: (1) Quantitative evaluation on TGVE and custom benchmarks using CLIP-consistency, flow-warping error, and editing accuracy; (2) Ablations on temporal window size and T-PEFT adapter placement; (3) User study comparing against Tokenflow, ground-truth edits, and per-frame ICEdit; (4) Scaling analysis showing data efficiency relative to prior video editing methods.

title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Transformer Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Sequences

Experiments: (1) Quantitative evaluation on TGVE and BalanceCC video editing benchmarks measuring CLIP-Text alignment, warping error (temporal consistency), and PSNR/SSIM; (2) Ablation studies comparing sliding window sizes, adapter placement, and temporal filtering strategies; (3) User study comparing against Pix2Video, TokenFlow, and ground-truth edited videos; (4) Efficiency analysis versus full fine-tuning video editing baselines.

title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation to Temporally Consistent Instruction-Based Video Editing

title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Temporal Editing via Diffusion Transformer In-Context Generation
description:

Additionally, we propose Frame-Selective Inference-Time Scaling, using a VLM to identify and prioritize temporally critical frames for noise sampling.

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Clip Modification

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequence Modification via Temporal Token Propagation
description:
Problem: Instruction-based editing for video remains underexplored — existing methods either process frames independently (causing temporal inconsistency) or require massive video-specific fine-tuning datasets. title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Clip Modification

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequence Modification via Temporal Attention Anchoring
description:

Applying per-frame editing independently produces flickering artifacts and semantic drift, while video-specific fine-tuning requires enormous datasets.

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Video Editing via Sparse Keyframe Conditioning in Diffusion Transformers
description:

Metrics cover temporal consistency (CLIP-T across frames), edit fidelity (text-image alignment), and background preservation (PSNR on unedited regions). title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequences
description:

title: Temporal In-Context Editing: Instruction-Based Video Editing via Sparse Keyframe In-Context Generation

title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Temporal Editing to Diffusion Transformer Video Models

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Transformers for Consistent Video Instruction Editing
