Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating temporal consistency as an additional in-context signal. Specifically, we propose TemporalICEdit, which concatenates (original_frame_t, edited_reference_frame, original_frame_t+k) as a triplet context window within a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or Open-Sora), enabling the model to infer both the editing instruction and temporal motion simultaneously. We introduce a Temporal Attention Anchor mechanism — a lightweight LoRA adaptation (~1% parameters) that biases cross-frame attention toward the edited reference frame to enforce style/content consistency without full fine-tuning. Additionally, we apply Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling across keyframes, using a VLM to select temporally coherent noise initializations before propagating edits to intermediate frames via flow-based interpolation.

Experiments: (1) Quantitative evaluation on TGVE and BalanceCC video editing benchmarks measuring temporal consistency (CLIP-T, flow warping error), editing fidelity (CLIP-Dir), and efficiency; (2) Ablation of context window size, LoRA rank, and keyframe selection strategies; (3) User study comparing against TokenFlow, Ground-A-Video, and video ControlNet baselines on instruction adherence and temporal smoothness.

title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequence Modification via Temporal Token Propagation
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates efficient single-image editing via in-context generation in DiTs, extending instruction-based editing to video sequences remains challenging due to temporal inconsistency—edits applied frame-by-frame produce flickering artifacts and lose coherence across the temporal dimension. Existing video editing methods require either massive fine-tuning datasets or sacrifice instruction comprehension quality.

Proposed Method: We extend the ICEdit in-context paradigm to video by introducing Temporal Token Propagation (TTP). Rather than treating each frame independently, we concatenate a reference (original frame, edited frame) pair as in-context tokens alongside a window of K consecutive frames within the DiT's attention mechanism. A lightweight temporal attention adapter (<<1% parameters) is trained on a small paired video-instruction dataset (~50K clips) to propagate edit semantics consistently across frames. We additionally propose a Temporal Early Filter that uses optical flow consistency as a cheap proxy signal to select coherent noise initializations across frames, extending ICEdit's inference-time scaling to the temporal domain.

Experiments: (1) Quantitative evaluation on TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks measuring temporal consistency (warping error), edit fidelity (CLIP score), and identity preservation (DINO similarity); (2) Ablation of context window size K and adapter parameter count; (3) User study comparing against Prompt2Prompt-video, TokenFlow, and ground-truth edits; (4) Efficiency comparison showing training data and compute requirements versus baselines.

title: In-Context Video Editing: Extending Instruction-Based Temporal Editing to Diffusion Transformer Video Models
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates remarkable efficiency for single-image instruction-based editing, video editing remains substantially harder due to temporal consistency requirements. Existing video editing methods either require expensive fine-tuning on large video datasets or fail to maintain coherent edits across frames. The in-context paradigm from ICEdit has not been explored for video, where temporal dependencies create unique challenges.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video diffusion transformers (e.g., CogVideoX, Wan) by designing a temporal in-context layout: the original video and edited video are concatenated along the temporal axis rather than spatial axis, enabling the model to attend across both source frames and target frames simultaneously. We introduce Temporal Consistency LoRA (TC-LoRA), a lightweight adapter trained on <50K video-instruction pairs that specifically regularizes inter-frame attention patterns during editing. We further adapt Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling to video by scoring candidate edits using a VLM that evaluates both instruction adherence AND temporal coherence metrics.

Experiments: (1) Benchmark on TGVE and custom video editing evaluation suite measuring edit accuracy, temporal consistency (CLIP-T, warping error), and background preservation; (2) Ablation of temporal concatenation strategies; (3) Comparison against Pix2Video, TokenFlow, and video ControlNet baselines; (4) Scaling analysis showing data efficiency relative to fully fine-tuned methods.

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequence Modification via Temporal Attention Binding
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates remarkable efficiency for single-image editing using in-context generation in DiTs, extending instruction-based editing to video sequences remains challenging due to temporal consistency requirements — naive frame-by-frame application of image editing methods produces flickering artifacts and identity drift across frames. Proposed Method: We propose TemporalICEdit, which extends the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating the original video frames and their edited counterparts as a joint temporal in-context sequence within video DiTs (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan). The key innovation is Temporal Attention Binding (TAB): we construct paired in-context tokens where the first half contains source frames and the second half contains progressively denoised edited frames, then introduce cross-frame attention constraints that enforce appearance consistency of non-edited regions while allowing instructed modifications to propagate coherently. We additionally apply parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, ~1% parameters) on a small dataset of ~5K video edit pairs. Planned Experiments: (1) Compare against frame-wise ICEdit, TokenFlow, and video instruct-pix2pix on TGVE and custom benchmarks using CLIP consistency, temporal warp error, and edit accuracy metrics; (2) Ablate TAB attention radius and LoRA rank; (3) User study on temporal coherence vs. editing fidelity tradeoff; (4) Demonstrate multi-shot editing with complex instructions like color changes, style transfer, and object replacement.

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Transformers to Consistent Video Editing via Temporal In-Context Frames
description:
Problem: Instruction-based video editing remains far more challenging than image editing due to the need for temporal consistency across frames. Existing video editing methods either require expensive per-video fine-tuning or struggle to maintain coherent edits throughout sequences. The success of ICEdit's in-context paradigm for images suggests a natural extension to video, but naive frame-by-frame application breaks temporal coherence.

Proposed Method: We propose TemporalICEdit, which reformulates video editing as a spatiotemporal in-context generation problem within a video DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or Wan2.1). The approach places the original video frames and a single edited reference frame (generated via ICEdit) as in-context conditioning tokens, allowing the model to propagate edits temporally without architectural changes. We introduce a Temporal Attention Anchoring mechanism that biases cross-frame attention toward the edited reference, and a lightweight LoRA adapter (1% parameters) trained on ~50K video-edit pairs to reinforce temporal consistency. Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling is extended to select temporally coherent noise initializations using a VLM that scores edit-consistency across sampled frame triplets.

Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and BalanceCC benchmarks measuring edit fidelity, temporal consistency (CLIP-T, warping error), and identity preservation. Ablations compare anchor-frame strategies and adapter sizes against baselines including TokenFlow, Ground-A-Video, and frame-wise ICEdit.

title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Editing via Temporal Attention Sharing
description:
Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates that in-context generation within DiTs enables efficient single-image editing, extending this paradigm to video remains unsolved. Video editing requires temporal consistency across frames, yet naively applying per-frame in-context editing produces flickering artifacts and incoherent object motion. Existing video editing methods require either massive video datasets or complex architectural changes.

Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by introducing TemporalEdit, which treats a video clip as a sequence of (original_frame, edited_frame) pairs arranged in a 2D spatiotemporal context window within a video DiT. Key innovations: (1) A temporal attention sharing mechanism where edited frames attend to both their original counterpart and neighboring edited frames, enforcing consistency without architectural modifications; (2) A lightweight temporal LoRA adapter (extending ICEdit's LoRA) trained on <50K video clips to learn inter-frame coherence; (3) Keyframe-guided inference-time scaling where VLMs evaluate temporal consistency scores across sampled trajectories, selecting coherent edits.

Experiments: Evaluate on TGVE and MotionBench benchmarks measuring temporal consistency (CLIP-T across frames), edit fidelity (per-frame CLIP-I), and user studies. Ablate temporal attention sharing vs. naive per-frame application. Compare against Tune-A-Video, TokenFlow, and ground-truth video editing baselines with 100x less training data.

title: TemporalEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Transformer Editing to Consistent Multi-Frame Video Sequences
description: Problem: Instruction-based video editing requires consistent modifications across temporally correlated frames, yet existing image editing methods like ICEdit operate frame-independently, producing flickering artifacts and temporal inconsistencies. Fine-tuning video diffusion models remains prohibitively expensive, and training-free approaches lack semantic coherence over time. Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by introducing a Temporal In-Context Window (TICW) mechanism within video Diffusion Transformers (e.g., CogVideoX, HunyuanVideo). Rather than conditioning on a single reference-target image pair, we construct an in-context sequence interleaving keyframes with their edited counterparts, enabling the model to propagate edits temporally via its native attention mechanism. We add lightweight temporal consistency adapters (LoRA on temporal attention layers only, ~0.5% parameters) trained on a small paired video editing dataset (~5K clips) generated via our image-editing pipeline applied to video keyframes. At inference, we apply a video-aware Early Filter Scaling strategy using a VLM that scores candidate denoised clips for instruction adherence and temporal coherence jointly. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and custom benchmarks measuring temporal consistency (CLIP-T coherence, warp error), instruction following (VQA scores), and compare against TokenFlow, Pix2Video, and ground-truth-supervised baselines with 100x more training data.

title: TemporalICEdit: Extending In-Context Diffusion Editing to Consistent Video Sequence Modification via Temporal Attention Anchoring
description: Problem: While ICEdit demonstrates impressive single-image editing with minimal training data, extending instruction-based editing to video sequences introduces the critical challenge of temporal consistency—edits must propagate coherently across frames without flickering or semantic drift, yet no efficient in-context paradigm exists for video editing at scale. Proposed Method: We extend the in-context editing paradigm to video by treating a sampled set of keyframes as a multi-image in-context 'gallery' within a video-capable DiT (e.g., CogVideoX or HunyuanVideo). We introduce Temporal Attention Anchoring (TAA), which ties the cross-frame attention maps of edited keyframes to intermediate frames during denoising, enforcing structural and appearance consistency without full video fine-tuning. A lightweight LoRA adapter (~1% parameters) is trained on ~50K instructed video clip pairs to align temporal coherence. We further apply the Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling strategy across candidate noise trajectories scored by a video-VLM for temporal quality. Experiments: We evaluate on TGVE and a newly curated InstructVideo-Bench covering 12 editing categories. Metrics include per-frame editing accuracy (CLIP score), temporal consistency (DINO feature variance), and human preference studies, comparing against TokenFlow, Ground-A-Video, and frame-wise ICEdit baselines.
